description: The any* family: eight micro, zero-dependency JavaScript/TypeScript formatters over native Intl — anywhen (dates), anyamount (numbers, money, units), anymany (lists), anyaround (region/language/currency names + flags), anylong (durations), anyplural (plurals), anyword (words/graphemes/sentences), anylocale (locale behaviour) — plus anyfamily (all in one) and anyfamily-react (hooks).
rules: Every package exports exactly one name, the package name. The bare call does the job; extras are statics on that name: anywhen.parts(date), anyword.count(text), anyamount.symbol('USD'), anylong.supported. There are no other runtime exports and no default export.
Options are always the last argument, a plain object. `locale` is a BCP 47 tag or an array used as a fallback chain; omit it to use the runtime locale.

Import from the package itself (`import { anywhen } from 'anywhen'`) or all eight from 'anyfamily'. In React use 'anyfamily-react': useAnywhen, useAnyamount, ... or useAnyfamily() for every function bound to the AnyfamilyProvider.
anylong needs Intl.DurationFormat (Node 23+, Baseline 2025), anyword needs Intl.Segmenter, anylocale needs Intl Locale Info; each exposes a `.supported` boolean to branch on.
Functions return plain strings (anyword returns a string[]; anylocale returns a record with lazy fields); `.parts()` returns Intl formatToParts-style arrays.
For SSR pass `now` to anywhen and an explicit `locale` everywhere so server and client render the same text.
